events.description: Mass anti-government uprisings in Kabul; Karmal appealed again to Moscow.
Moscow leadership reportedly considered withdrawal of troops, but Ustinov, Andropov and possibly Gromyko opposed.
LCST began active operations against armed opposition in Kunar Province, after Moscow's order.
Replacement of reservist officers with regular officers completed.
Mass anti-government uprisings in Kabul at end of February 1980, prompting another appeal from Karmal to the Soviet government.
Moscow ordered Soviet forces in Afghanistan to begin active operations to destroy armed opposition formations together with the DRA Army.
LCST formations began operations in Kunar Province.
Soviet leadership considered withdrawing troops from Afghanistan but decided against it, with Ustinov and Andropov opposed.
Replacement of reservist officers with regular officers in the LCST completed; sergeants and soldiers by March (1981); 33.5 thousand replaced.

key_claims: Soviet leaders initially intended troops not to engage in combat against the Afghan opposition except in self-defense or to rescue advisers.
After the Feb 1980 Kabul uprising and Karmal's appeal, Moscow ordered active operations with the DRA Army against the opposition.
LCST operations began in Kunar Province in March 1980.
Brezhnev reportedly considered withdrawal in Feb 1980 but Ustinov, Andropov and possibly Gromyko opposed it.
Decision to stay led to the Soviets' involvement in the Afghan civil war.
Reservists were replaced by regular personnel; 33,500 people were replaced.
